stories.headline: White Sox lose 9-6 to Rockies, end chances of winning AL Central
stories.summary: — The Chicago White Sox had their hopes of winning the AL Central dashed when Hunter Goodman hit his 40th and 41st homers to lift the Colorado Rockies in a 9-6 win Saturday night.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — The Chicago White Sox had their hopes of winning the AL Central dashed when Hunter Goodman hit his 40th and 41st homers to lift the Colorado Rockies in a 9-6 win Saturday night.


The White Sox needed to beat the Rockies to stay alive in the division race after the Cleveland Guardians won 11-5 at Kansas City on Saturday to take a two-game lead on the season's penultimate day.


Chicago will be the final AL wild card and will play on the road against the AL West winner in a three-game Wild Card Series beginning Tuesday. The race between the Texas Rangers and Houston Astros for the West crown will come down to the season's last day.


Chicago is the first team to earn a playoff berth after consecutive 100-loss seasons.


The Rockies won for just the fourth time in 21 games. They improved to a major league-worst 58-103 after losing a club-record 119 last season.


The White Sox led or were tied for first in the AL Central from July 4 until Sept. 16.


Ryan Feltner (7-10) gave up three hits in 3 2/3 innings in relief for Colorado.


The Rockies went ahead 3-0 in the first. Davis Martin (9-8) committed a fielding error before allowing three singles, a walk and two earned runs while recording just two outs.


Goodman homered off Noah Schultz in the third, becoming the first Rockies player to hit 40 homers since Nolan Arenado in 2019. Ezequiel Tovar added his 13th homer in the fourth to make it 5-2. Goodman added a three-run shot in the Rockies’ four-run ninth.


Andrew Benintendi hit a three-run homer in the ninth for Chicago. Brenton Doyle and Luisangel Acuña also homered.


The White Sox had their chances. They put runners at the corners in the sixth, but Feltner struck out pinch hitter Colson Montgomery to end the inning. Montgomery extended the season record for strikeouts to 225.


Up next
LHP Anthony Kay (9-9, 4.53 ERA) is set to start for the White Sox in Sunday’s regular season finale. LHP Kyle Freeland (4-11, 6.58) will pitch for Colorado.

stories.headline: Pass or fail? Grading every AFL team's season based on preseason expectations
stories.summary: Make finals, win the flag, or avoid the bottom four ... we gave each team a pass mark coming into the 2026 season. So how did every club go?
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL home-and-away season has come to an end, so it's time to start taking stocks of every team's year. We take a look back at our preseason expectations to work out if your club passed or failed in 2026.

This will be updated as every team's season finishes, or every preseason question has been answered.

READ: Our preseason pass marks - catch up on what we said here

Adelaide
2026 pass mark: Avoid regression and WIN a final

Record: 15-8 (6th)

PASS: Well, it looked dicey for a bit there in the fourth quarter of Adelaide's win over the Bulldogs, but the Crows have kicked the monkey off the back in winning their first final since 2017. They also avoided a catastrophic freefall after going out in straight sets as the minor premiers in 2025. Overall, it's had to gauge what Adelaide's ceiling is; a 15-8 home-and-away season record was good but not great, and beating the Bulldogs at home in an elimination final is expected. What's probably not expected is beating the reigning premiers in a semifinal at the Gabba. Overall, we give them a pass, but given the top-end talent on the list, we'll be expecting even more in 2027.

Brisbane
2026 pass mark: Avoid a culture nosedive

Record: 16-7 (3rd)

PASS: It's hard to tell from the outside looking in what effect any off-field drama had on the list both going into the season and then during it. But what we can assess is the way they performed on the field regardless of the noise. At times, it seemed the three-peat just wasn't doable, think conceding 13 goals in one quarter to the Giants, for example. It all culminated in an epic finals series; smashed by the Swans, cruising past the Crows, surviving the Hawks in preliminary final epic, and then coming from absolutely nowhere to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat on Grand Final day. The one thing we know is these players just get it done for each other, no matter the circumstances.

Carlton
2026 pass mark: Play in a wildcard final

Record: 12-10-1 (10th)

PASS: This has been a truly remarkable year for Carlton, who started 1-8 (with the club's only win in that time coming against Richmond) and sacked the coach before the halfway point of the season. Since then? Josh Fraser took over as intering, the team went 11-2-1 (the best record in that time of any club), appointed Fraser full-time, then won a wildcard game. To say it's one of the most bizarre seasons in recent memory might actually be underselling it! Considering our preseason expectations, it's definitely a 'pass', but could it have been more resounding had Fraser been in charge the whole year?!

Collingwood
2026 pass mark: Begin the transition to the next era

Record: 12-9-2 (9th)

PASS: It was forced for the most part, Collingwood playing through the season with a lengthy injury list largely filled by an experienced group of players, but several new Pies were blooded in an up-and-down 2026 campaign which ended in a wildcard defeat. They've found a couple of potential stars in Sam Swadling and Oscar Steene, and got valuable games into Ed Allan and Charlie West, while Harvey Harrison came back from an ACL layoff, and Will Hayes and Angus Anderson got some exposure. What they'll be able to achieve as a group with club greats Scott Pendlebury and Steele Sidebottom departing remains to be seen, but we definitely witnessed a gradual transition to the next era.

Essendon
2026 pass mark: Have a winning record post the mid-year bye

Record: 2-21 (18th)

FAIL: It's been a dire year for the Bombers, who sacked Brad Scott after 10 games and have been barely treading water since. Unfortunately there hasn't been too much silver lining, except maybe getting crucual games into Sullivan Robey, Dyson Sharp, Nate Caddy, Isaac Kako, and other youngsters. There's a vacuum of on-field leadership at Essendon, and it's something the club needs to address in the offseason. It's going to be a dark few years -- making good choices with list management now could pay off in the long term, and Robey, Sharp, and Caddy look like 'ticks' so far.

Fremantle
2026 pass mark: Win a final

Record: 19-4 (1st)

PASS: It's been a dominant season for the Dockers. Minor premiers. Five players selected to the All-Australian team. But the question everyone wondered was whether or not they could win a final. Last year, Fremantle was upset by the Suns in an elimination at Optus Stadium. This year, the Hawks came to town and humbled them in a qualifying final, heaping an enormous amount of pressure on them for a must-win semifinal against Geelong. Justin Longmuir and his troops can breathe a huge sigh of relief after overcoming the Cats in a shootout, then Sydney in a prelim. A shattering way to end it all on Grand Final day? Absolutely, but this team still took massive strides and they're not going anywhere.

Geelong
2026 pass mark: Lock up a top four spot

Record: 15-8 (6th)

FAIL: The Cats proved the Grand Final curse might not be a real thing .. sort of. Teams that lose a Grand Final by 40+ points almost never win a final the following year, but that history didn't stop them from knocking off the Blues in an elimination final. Geelong's season ended on Friday night with a loss to Fremantle in the west, meaning no return to the top four (we would have counted a prelim finish as a top four spot). So, technically it's a fail, but it's not one that should have Cats fans majorly concerned ahead of season 2027.

Gold Coast
2026 pass mark: Reach a preliminary final

Record: 9-14 (13th)

FAIL: Was Gold Coast the most disappointing team in 2026? Yeah, Essendon exists, but the Suns had sky-high expectations after winning a final last season and attracting Christian Petracca to the Coast. Now, star forward Ben King looks certain to leave, the midfield mix isn't working, and Damien Hardwick is under immense pressure in just his third year in charge. The upside is they should have a 'soft' draw in 2027 and bounce straight back into the finals.

GWS
2026 pass mark: Win a final

Record: 10-13 (12th)

FAIL: Adam Kingsley's side had higher expectations in 2026 and failed to deliver. Injuries didn't help the cause, and to be fair, with so many stars sidelined, what can really be expected? That doesn't mean the year isn't a disappointing one, Kingsley even said so in his post-match presser after the loss to the Crows. Particularly when you look at the results more specifically; wins against the Cats, Dockers, Dees, Lions, and Hawks, but losses against the lowly Eagles and wooden spoon-winning Bombers. They were far from healthy, but they were still way too inconsistent.

Hawthorn
2026 pass mark: Don't throw away the season

Record: 15-6-2 (4th)

PASS: If not for a controversial holding-the-ball free kick in the final minute of Saturday evening's preliminary final against Brisbane, the Hawks would be playing in this year's Grand Final. It's been a remarkable season for Sam Mitchell's side, the club taking significant strides forward despite failing to land Essendon star Zach Merrett during the offseason and there being an overwhelming feeling 2026 could be a wasted year. Adding Merrett to the fold could just about put this side into premiership favouritism for next season. This isn't just a pass, it's a pass with flying colours.

Melbourne
2026 pass mark: Avoid re-entering the dark, dark times

Record: 15-8 (7th)

PASS: Melbourne exceeded the expectations of probably all but the nuffiest of Dees fans. Widely tipped to have a regression season after losing stars Christian Petracca and Clayton Oliver in the offseason, the Demons found an attacking edge that made them 'fun and dangerous'. They reached finals again, almost finished top four, and you could mount the case Steven King has been coach of the year. Sure, the club and its fans has a right to feel disappointed following that wildcard loss to Carlton, all after only narrowly missing the top six. But the season as a whole is a pass, there can be no doubting that.

North Melbourne
2026 pass mark: Make a wildcard final

Record: 9-14 (14th)

FAIL: Was this slightly lofty? Maybe. The facts are North won nine games, four more than in 2025, and showed significant statistical improvement. It's a failed season only because they need to have more lofty expectations as a club, but that doesn't mean they haven't taken steps forward. They were largely competitive in more games against tough opponents -- think the recent 15-point loss to the Cats, the 16-point defeat to Hawthorn down in Tassie, four-point loss to the Pies, eight-point loss to the Swans earlier in the year. They were at least in the wildcard hunt for the majority of the season, but the next step is obviously being able to beat more of those sides above them. Their deficiencies are clear; 18th for intercept possessions, 15th for opposition scores per inside 50, 16th for inside 50s but No. 1 for marks when they get it in there. Get another quality key defender, and better conversion, and who knows what they can do in 2027.

Port Adelaide
2026 pass mark: Re-sign Zak Butters or land a record-breaking trade package

Record: 7-16 (15th)

FAIL: Obviously, we'll update this after he makes his call in the exit meeting this week. But it's not looking promising for Port Adelaide fans. It's been a season-long distraction of 'will he, won't he' and it's taken away from some rather encouraging performances from this side. Nine wins last year, and seven wins this year under first-year coach Josh Carr isn't disastrous, and single-digit losses to West Coast (Round 3), Hawthorn (Round 6), Adelaide (Round 8), Western Bulldogs (Round 9), and Sydney (Round 14) showed they had opportunities to win even more games. Their percentage was a tick off 100 with six weeks to go in the season, a good sign of a competitive group. A harsh 'fail', but given the criteria...

Richmond
2026 pass mark: Build on last year's semi-successful season

Record: 3-20 (17th)

FAIL: Five wins in 2025, three wins in 2026 (two over West Coast). In terms of rebuilding teams, it's not the end of the world, but you simply cannot say they built on last year's result. Fans are also starting to get a bit restless with Adem Yze, whose 10-59 record (14.5%) at Richmond is objectively very poor. What we will ask is this: would Norm Smith, Leigh Matthews, and peak Clarko combined have been able to squeeze more wins out of the list? We doubt it. Rebuilding coaches always get the short end of the stick, but everyone knew this would be a tough slog. It's a clear fail, but stick with them.

St Kilda
2026 pass mark: Give Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera a reason to stay

Record: 10-13 (11th)

FAIL: Hmm... Ross, this was supposed to be the year to convince your star St Kilda is the place to be. You splashed the cash, brought in a host of experience from other clubs in the hopes to rise at least into an (expanded!) finals with a wildcard spot, and instead you're left in the land of mediocrity, again. Same old, same old. That doesn't mean you don't have time, but a lot's going to need to change for the better before Wanganeen-Milera's head gets turned. In fairness, injuries haven't helped, but players want flags. They want to contend. They want to be there in September. If I were Nas' agent, I'd be telling him to put the pen away and start listening to other offers...

Sydney
2026 pass mark: Be alive during preliminary final week

Record: 18-5 (2nd)

PASS: We can already tick this off, and credit to the Swans, how the club, its leaders, and the players have handled themselves in the wake of the 'Pullman Five' episode has been exemplary. Defeating the reigning premiers in a qualifying final when not many gave them a chance means they've hit their pass mark, and they may well have more to say in 2026. Regardless of how you feel about Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey and co., how the club has responded on and off the field since has just about been faultless.

West Coast
2026 pass mark: Avoid the wooden spoon

Record: 4-19 (16th)

PASS: There's still pressure on Andrew McQualter and the club to start winning more games, but broadly, this has been a stepping stone season in the rebuild. Getting crucial games into Willem Duursma, Cooper Duff-Tytler, Bo Allan, Josh Lindsay, and Tom Gross among others has been a big tick, while Jobe Shanahan (29 goals) has taken enough of a step to suggest he'll be a long-term No. 1 key forward and partner for Jake Waterman for the Eagles. Four wins, 16th on the ladder? Not great, but a reluctant 'pass' nonetheless. The expectations will rise in 2027.

Western Bulldogs
2026 pass mark: Finish the home and away season in the top four

Record: 13-9-1 (8th)

FAIL: Another year, another middle of the road finish for the Bulldogs, who, like Carlton, play finals by virtue of the wildcard. Had it been a top eight? A big fail. But, considering our preseason expectations, they've still fallen short. Sure, there have been injuries to key players throughout the year, but all clubs face similar hurdles, and the Bulldogs have shown again they're just a middle-of-the-road side that lacks quality depth. Were our expectations too high? Very possibly, but we weren't alone in hoping the Dogs could finally finish top four after the home-and-away season under Luke Beveridge.

stories.headline: England boss Thomas Tuchel: Potential Man City punishments not a distraction in Spain defeat
stories.summary: Thomas Tuchel has insisted Manchester City's potential punishment for breaching Premier League financial rules was not a distraction for his England players in Saturday's 3-2 Nations League defeat to Spain.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Thomas Tuchel has insisted Manchester City's potential punishment for breaching Premier League financial rules was not a distraction for his England players in Saturday's 3-2 Nations League defeat to Spain.

A source told ESPN on Friday that City are expected to be found guilty in the vast majority of the 115 charges relating to alleged misconduct between 2009 and 2018.

City trio Marc Guéhi, Nico O'Reilly and Elliot Anderson all started at Wembley barely 24 hours after news of the likely guilty verdict broke.

City continue to deny all charges and the Premier League declined to comment when contacted by ESPN.

England captain Harry Kane said there had been a "discussion" within the group about City's situation while both Guéhi and O'Reilly made individual mistakes, as Spain came from 2-1 down to win through substitute Mikel Oyarzabal's 74th-minute strike.

Asked whether the City situation could be an issue during the international break, Tuchel said: "Not for me but I can imagine maybe for the Manchester City players but for me not and I will not comment on that because it is an ongoing court case so I will not give any comment.

"I didn't make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I hear the news as the latest person in camp. I was just thinking about Spain and training and meetings and media meetings and individual meetings. Not for me. For the players, they have more time than me, they have one training session. I can imagine they talk about it. It is good they do. I didn't feel they were distracted."

Speaking to ITV, Kane said: "There was a discussion, but at the end of the day when we're with England, that's been a big plus for us, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week."

- Hamilton, Olley: Spain expose England's shortcomings in breathtaking Wembley comeback

- Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

England fell behind after just two minutes as Guehi gifted Lamine Yamal the chance to open the scoring. Anthony Gordon equalised before Kane's deflected header put the Three Lions 2-1 in front at the break.

Kane missed a penalty to put England 3-1 up on 54 minutes before world champions Spain responded as Álex Baena and Oyarzabal both came off the bench to score in a thrilling League A Group 3 opener.

"I think in this moment it [Kane's penalty] would have been the decisive punch to get this full momentum and full belief into our match with a two-goal advantage," Tuchel said.

"Couldn't do it, made unfortunately another technical mistake that cost us, and then the momentum shifted again. We conceded one goal from open play that we should absolutely defend better because they play through the middle.

"The result is not what we wanted. I think we could have won it, so we have to live with it, recover from it, learn from it, do what we did good on the same level, and reduce and improve our own mistakes."

stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 3 inactives: Caleb Williams out, Puka Nacua uncertain, Darnold a go
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists.

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 3 Buzz

Week 3 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 3

Biggest concerns heading into Week 3
Players with early starts

DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore was limited Wednesday and wearing a noncontact jersey. He then missed practice Thursday before logging another limited session with the noncontact jersey Friday. He is questionable heading into Week 3 -- and truly could go in either direction, although it's worth noting that Moore has not missed a game since 2020. If he's active, fantasy managers should plan to start him, even if he is somewhat limited. If he sits, expect Khalil Shakir to see more work.

Keon Coleman, WR, Bills (ankle): Coleman also missed practice this week. He was able to log a limited session Friday and is also questionable heading into Sunday. If Coleman sits, Joshua Palmer and Skyler Bell will be the next options. The main target for Buffalo would be Dalton Kincaid. Some potential outside replacement options for any missing Bills are Devaughn Vele, Denzel Boston, Josh Downs, Adonai Mitchell*, and Dontayvion Wicks.

*See below.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After missing practice Thursday, Coker returned in a limited fashion Friday -- his second practice of the week. He is questionable for Week 3. It's worth noting that Coker missed practice last week and still ended up suiting up (and performing adequately for fantasy managers). He has seen nine targets in both games this season. In fact, his usage is very similar to Tetairoa McMillan, only Coker is seeing a higher number of efficient targets. If Coker suits up against the Browns, he is in play. If he sits, some replacement options would be the same as those listed above for Coleman.

Malik Nabers, WR, Giants (shoulder): Nabers suffered his injury during "Monday Night Football" but was able to return to the field. He did pop up on the practice report this week but was able to log in full practices and is good to go for Week 3. Though he is a more volatile fantasy option with Jameis Winston under center, he still brings enough upside to be viewed as a WR2.

Adonai Mitchell, WR, Jets (finger): The Jets receiver was added to the practice report Thursday and logged two limited practices. He is questionable for Week 3. Mitchell saw a team-high 12 targets in Week 2 and is a popular streaming option in Week 3 against the Lions, who have allowed the most WR yards this season. If he suits up, he can be used as an upside WR3/flex play.

Michael Pittman Jr., WR, Steelers (foot): After missing Week 2, Pittman was able to log limited practices this week. That puts him on the right side of questionable. Even so, Pittman is nothing more than a low-floor flex option due to the struggling Steelers passing attack. Our main list of streaming options mentioned previously are all receivers I would rather play than Pittman.

Jadarian Price, RB, Seahawks (chest): Price was limited at practice to start the week but got in a full practice and Friday and is good to go Sunday. The Seahawks face the Commanders, who have been "middle of the road" against RBs. However, game script should largely be on Seattle's side. As such, Price is an RB2 play who can be started over Travis Etienne Jr., Warren, Rhamondre Stevenson and any Broncos RB. If he were to relapse and need to sit, Emanuel Wilson (who turned 21 carries into 92 yards last week) would slide into place as a strong RB2.

Sam Darnold, QB, Seahawks (glute): The Super Bowl-winning QB returned to practice this week and will play against the Commanders. Though him playing elevates those around him, and Darnold is still a QB2 for fantasy purposes, I would not start him ahead of Tyler Shough, Kyler Murray, Bryce Young and C.J. Stroud.

Tyjae Spears, RB, Titans (ankle): Tennessee's passing-downs back did not practice to open the week but was able to log in a limited session on Friday. While he has a chance to play he is questionable and truly seems up in the air heading into Week 3. Spears has handled the bulk of passing-down opportunities while splitting snaps with Tony Pollard. If Spears sits, that will catapult Pollard into the flex range and, in that case, you can consider using him over the likes of Stevenson, RJ Harvey, Blake Corum and any Commanders RB.

Players with late starts

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (hamstring): Flowers exited action early in Week 1 and then missed Week 2. He was able to return to practice Friday, giving him a chance to play in Week 3. It's worth noting that he also logged a limited practice last Friday but ultimately sat. It would be a nice surprise if Flowers were able to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place. If he sits, Rashod Bateman will once again be the WR1 for the Ravens and be in play as an upside WR3.

Brock Bowers, TE, Raiders (knee): The star tight end is questionable for Week 3. Bowers logged two limited practices to start the week. He did not practice Friday, but that was "part of the plan," according to Klint Kubiak. If Bowers plays, he should start for fantasy managers, unless you also happen to have Dalton Kincaid on your roster. Even if Bowers were to be on some sort of snap count, the upside is worth the risk. Fantasy managers already have had a backup plan in place regarding Bowers and should do so once again heading into Sunday.

Aaron Jones Sr., RB, Vikings (knee): Jones missed practice to start the week but was able to return (limited) Thursday and finally was elevated to full Friday. He no longer carries an injury designation and should play. This is something fantasy managers should get used to, as the veteran will likely have more midweek rest days in the future. Jones played on over 80% of snaps and had 23 carries in Week 2. That makes him an RB2/flex option worth getting into your lineups this week.

Travis Etienne Jr., RB, Saints (hamstring): After being limited to start the practice week, Etienne returned to full participation Friday. He no longer carries an injury destination and will play in Week 3. There's still concern that he was out-touched by Alvin Kamara last week 14-10. The inconsistent usage has him in the RB3/flex range. Some options to play over him are Bhayshul Tuten, Quinshon Judkins or Aaron Jones.

Mike Evans, WR, 49ers (hip): Evans exited early in Week 2 and missed practice to start the week. Ian Rapoport reported that there is a "good chance" that, if Evans returns to practice, he will play this week. If he suits up, he is a WR2 with some injury risk.

Players going Sunday night

Puka Nacua, WR, Rams (groin): After missing Week 2 due to a groin injury, Nacua has missed practice all week. He is doubtful for Week 3. Sean McVay did say Friday that, barring a setback, Nacua should return in Week 4. His absence means more volume for Davante Adams, but also likely means being matched up more against Pat Surtain II.

Assuming Nacua sits, the top replacement option on the Rams would be Terrance Ferguson (in the flex). There is no Rams receiver that fantasy managers should trust other than Adams. Some alternative streaming options to aim for here are Romeo Doubs, Quentin Johnston, and Malik Washington.

J.K. Dobbins/RJ Harvey, RB, Broncos: Dobbins left last week with leg cramps, while Harvey missed the game due to a hamstring issue. Both logged full practices Thursday and Friday and do not carry an injury designation headed into "Sunday Night Football." I would expect the work to be distributed between the two like it was in Week 1, when Dobbins was the lead runner and Harvey played the bulk of passing downs. Both would come in as low-floor flex options due to the uncertain usage and matchup against a tough Rams defensive front. Both appear to be usable flex options for the foreseeable future with Jonah Coleman on IR.
Players going on Monday night

Saquon Barkley, RB, Eagles (stinger): Barkley suffered a stinger in Week 2 and exited after just five touches. He was able to return to practice this week, so the expectation is that he will suit up this week. If he's in the Eagles huddle, he should be in your fantasy lineup -- especially in this matchup. However, given that the game is Monday, fantasy managers need to have a backup plan in place from that game. Tank Bigsby is the ideal option, but Wicks could be a pivot as long as you put Barkley in your flex spot.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (knee): Monangai has been dealing with knee issues since the summer and, while it cost him some practice time in past weeks, he has still been able to play. He returned to practice Friday and the expectation is that he will be able to play this week. If he does, he is a RB3/flex option. Last season against the Eagles, he went for 130 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): Smith missed practice to start the week but returned on Friday, putting him on track to play Monday. If Smith plays for the Eagles, he plays for fantasy managers, especially in this matchup. If he were to sit, Dontayvion Wicks would be the Eagles No. 1 target. He is already a flex option with Dallas Goedert set to miss extended time.

Cairo Santos, K, Bears (right hip): The Bears kicker has not practiced this week and is on the wrong side of questionable heading into Week 3. With Williams expected out, fantasy managers should be looking to replace Santos with a kicker from another team. Some options are Chase McLaughlin, Will Reichard, Harrison Mevis and Tyler Bass.

-->

Ruled out before Sunday
Caleb Williams, QB, Bears (hamstring): Williams is "week-to-week" after getting hurt in Week 2. He has been ruled out for Monday Night Football against the Eagles. Backup QB Tyson Bagent is in the league's concussion protocol, but was able to practice on Saturday. If he cannot go, that would leave Case Keenum as the starter. The loss of Williams makes all Bears pass catchers volatile starts this week.

Jonah Coleman, RB, Broncos: All three Broncos RBs appeared on the injury report this week. Coleman is dealing with an ankle injury and has been ruled out for Week 3. He was placed on IR and will miss at least four games.
Jonathon Brooks, RB, Panthers (groin): Brooks has been placed on IR with an injury that will sideline him at least six weeks, per Ian Rapoport. Brooks has all the talent in the world but unfortunately has not been able to stay healthy in his NFL career. Feel free to stash him. In the interim, this leaves Chuba Hubbard as the Panthers starter. He should handle much more work than previously anticipated. Hubbard is a firm RB2, with the upside to finish certain weeks as a RB1.

Nico Collins, WR, Texans (hamstring): Houston's star receiver has missed practice all week and will be out again for Week 3. In his absence last week, Dalton Schultz saw 14 targets. Xavier Hutchinson was the top-targeted wideout with nine. Schultz is a strong TE1 start. To replace Collins, fantasy managers should look outside of the Texans huddle and to our list of top replacement options -- Vele, Boston, Downs, Mitchell and Wicks.

Alec Pierce, WR, Colts (heel): Pierce aggravated his injury last week and has been placed on IR. He will be out "several weeks" according to Ian Rapoport, who reported that Pierce will attempt to rehab the injury. If so, he could return "midseason". Pierce should be stashed on your fantasy team's IR in any leagues that allow the option. In leagues that do not, he is not a must-hold guy.

David Njoku, TE, Chargers (knee): Njoku has landed on IR due to a fibula injury. Teammate and fellow TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) has avoided the IR for now but is banged up and out for Week 3. That leaves Oronde Gadsden as the Chargers' top tight end and pushes him back into fantasy relevance. While he is more of a streaming option for those in need, he has the upside of potentially blossoming into a TE1 with more usage.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (ankle): The rookie WR got hurt in Week 2 and has missed practice this week. He has been ruled out for Week 3. Though Douglas is more of a depth piece for fantasy managers, his absence means more opportunity for Malik Washington and Chris Bell. Still, in a tough matchup against the Chiefs, managers should be looking outside of Miami if they need a replacement.

Jaxson Dart, QB, Giants (knee): Dart suffered an injury that may potentially force season-ending surgery. In his absence, Jameis Winston, who struggled mightily in Week 2, will start. Fantasy managers can still use any of Nabers, Isaiah Likely and Cam Skattebo -- they just come with a lot more volatility.

Dallas Goedert, TE, Eagles (knee): Goedert has an MCL sprain that could sideline him for a few weeks. The Eagles did add Zach Ertz following the injury -- and perhaps he could become fantasy-relevant again. For the time being, fantasy managers should look elsewhere. Some replacement options that could be available are Schultz, Ferguson, Juwan Johnson, Darren Waller and Hunter Henry.

Rico Dowdle, RB, Steelers (toe): Dowdle exited early in Week 2 and was seen in a boot to start the week. He did not practice and is out for Week 3. With him out, Jaylen Warren -- who himself is questionable with a shoulder injury -- should see a boost both in volume and fantasy value for the week. Warren should handle the bulk of running opportunities and has already been featured in the passing game, averaging five targets per game. The volume keeps him in play as an RB2/flex option.

Jayden Daniels, QB, Commanders (elbow): Daniels dislocated his left elbow in Week 2. It's the same injury that he suffered last season. The good news is Daniels has avoided the IR -- at least so far -- but he has been ruled out for Week 3. Marcus Mariota will be the "next man up" but he is only in play in superflex leagues. Even there, against the Seahawks, you should look to avoid him. The loss of Daniels dings the values of all Commanders receiving options, making Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs "sits" in this extremely tough matchup.

stories.headline: Sources: Bulls to trade Dillingham to Hornets for Buddy Hield
stories.summary: The Chicago Bulls are trading Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Saturday.
stories.body:
The Chicago Bulls are trading Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Saturday.

Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft and still just 21 years old, is being traded less than a year after landing in Chicago at the trade deadline last season. He appeared in 30 games for the Bulls, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

Dillingham could have a chance for a larger role in Charlotte, which traded longtime starting guard LaMelo Ball to the Timberwolves earlier this offseason. News of this trade comes just one day after the Hornets announced that second-year guard Kon Knueppel has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

The Hornets create a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal.

Hield spent less than a week with the Hornets, who acquired the veteran sharpshooter from the Atlanta Hawks for Dorian Finney-Smith. Hield, known as a positive and high-energy player, has history with Bulls executive vice president Bryson Graham from their time together in New Orleans.

Dillingham has one more year via a team option on his rookie contract before hitting restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Hield has a player option worth around $10 million for the 2027-28 season.

stories.headline: Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli has been Mercedes' clear-cut No. 1 driver this season, but George Russell's persistence was rewarded with a win in Baku on Saturday
stories.body:
George Russell might look back on winning Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as a breakthrough moment in his 2026 season. That's not to say it will be a turning point in his title fight with teammate Kimi Antonelli -- by his own admission, Russell's championship chances hang by no more than a thread -- but instead the moment in which he was rewarded for keeping the faith in his own ability.

The 2026 Formula 1 season to date has been a bruising one for the Mercedes driver. After going into the year as the title favorite, it quickly became apparent that his more junior teammate held the edge in terms of outright performance. For a handful of races, Russell was able to blame bad luck -- which was undoubtedly present at a number of races, including Japan, Canada and Monaco -- but by the summer break it was increasingly clear that Antonelli's growing lead in the championship was built more on outright performance than random circumstance.

By that point of the year, and to his credit, Russell had recognized his own shortcomings. He returned from F1's month-long summer break knowing he would have to make changes to his driving style, no matter how uncomfortable they might feel. Under the previous set of regulations, which smothered the cars in downforce, Russell's high-commitment, high-entry-speed approach to corners was rewarded with a car that could meet his demands.

Arguably, it not only gave him the edge over Antonelli during the Italian's rookie season, but also over his previous Mercedes teammate, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton. The only downside was that Mercedes' engineers never truly got their collective heads around the previous set of regulations to provide Russell with a car capable of using those inherent strengths to fight for the title.

The introduction of a new formula this year -- one with less downforce, narrower tires and the added complication of managing electrical energy around the lap -- has seen Mercedes return to the front of the grid, but Russell's natural driving style fail to sync. As recently as Wednesday's news conference in Baku, Russell admitted Antonelli, who is typically later on the brakes and more comfortable in reacting to the car's movement underneath him, had "the perfect driving style for these cars," whereas his "isn't working as well."

The difference in performance between Russell and Antonelli has been particularly marked over a race distance this year. Antonelli can eke more performance from the tires over their lifespan, whereas Russell's pace has tended to drop off over a race distance -- even at circuits where he has been a match for his teammate in qualifying.

As Russell has pointed out multiple times in the past few races, Formula 1 is not like tennis or golf where an athlete can spend endless hours training away from a competitive environment to hone their technique. The only opportunity Russell has had to adapt his driving style to his 2026 Mercedes is during races, and it became his main focus every time he got behind the wheel.

"It feels great, to be honest," he said of victory in Baku. "I'm very proud of the resilience that I and my close group of engineers have shown during the tough periods this year because there's been a lot of hard work to overcome some of the challenges, to adapt my driving style to suit this new car better.

"And F1 is so tough, you don't get opportunities to practice this, and finally it's coming to me a bit more intuitively than it once did, and I'm gaining confidence. And especially on circuits like this, it just allows you to eke out that little bit more on the brakes, get that little bit closer to the walls, and it's been a flawless weekend."

The challenge facing Russell in recent races has not only been technical, but also mental. While Russell has been working on making changes to his driving style after the summer break, Antonelli has extended his lead in the championship with victories at Monza and the Madring.

It would have been easy to lose heart as Russell's title hopes slipped beyond his grasp, but he continued to believe in his underlying potential to return to the top step of the podium.

"I think I never lost that faith in myself, even through tough moments I knew there was a reason why I was off the pace," he said. "It wasn't like I just suddenly forgot how to drive, and I knew I would be able to find it again. I just had to be patient. So, I feel confident. You know, it's been four races since the break. I've been on the front row in three of them, three podiums from the four races. I feel I can fight for victory week in, week out now."

For all Russell's evident progress in Baku, there was one thing that was missing from Saturday's victory: a competitive Antonelli to measure himself against.

After a hydraulic issue curtailed his Thursday practice sessions in Azerbaijan, Antonelli never seemed to hit his stride around the street circuit this weekend. In what appeared to be an attempt to overcompensate for his lack of performance, he clipped the barrier at Turn 1 on his second hot lap in qualifying, which ruled him out of the rest of the session and left him 16th on the grid for Saturday's race.

Starting so far back in the pack, the championship leader opted not to push the limits in the race, and his restraint was rewarded with 10 points for a fifth-place finish.

"This weekend was my worst of the year by far in terms of performance," Antonelli said after the race. "I wasn't there. I wasn't really present, especially with what happened so early on, and just didn't take the same risks, especially after qualifying. Today was more 'damage-safe mode' instead of full attack."

Driving in any kind of "safe mode" is not in Antonelli's DNA and it is incredibly unlikely Russell will come up against a similarly uncompetitive version of his teammate again this season. It's the main reason why Russell's Baku victory should not be seen as a turning point in the championship, and is better viewed as a step in his own progress toward a more competitive version of himself for the remainder of this season and 2027.

How big that step truly is will likely become clear as Antonelli gets back up to speed at the variety of circuit types that make up the rest of the season. It was notable that, prior to Baku, Russell had often drawn parallels between his struggles and those of McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who, just like Russell, has been outperformed by his teammate since the introduction of the 2026 regulations.

"I think Oscar and I have been dealing with similar sort of struggles this year," Russell said on Wednesday. "The car is very different, the tires are different, power unit aside, and what's probably worked so well in the past for the two of us, and maybe a couple of other drivers on the grid, this year isn't working as well."

It's perhaps no coincidence, then, that up until his lap-40 mistake at Turn 1, Piastri was trending toward one of his best performances of the season in Baku. Could it be that the same driving style traits that have limited Piastri and Russell so often this year were in some way less restrictive around one of F1's most notorious outlier circuits? Or that the driving styles that have served Antonelli and Lando Norris so well elsewhere this year were in some way neutered this weekend? The return of a more conventional circuit in Malaysia's Sepang next weekend will likely hold the answer.

In the meantime, however, Russell deserves to revel in his success. The triple achievement of pole position, victory and fastest lap -- known as a grand slam in racing circles -- doesn't come along very often in a Formula 1 career and is always proof of a weekend spent at the top of a driver's game.

"I think it's probably my first grand slam in Formula 1 and, for sure, the most dominant weekend I've had in my career," Russell said. "So that has come at a really great moment.

"And also to achieve it on a circuit that requires so much commitment and confidence, I'm really proud of because I think it would have been very easy for me to lose the faith this season. Not necessarily about winning the championship, but in terms of my ability, and that never happened."

stories.headline: Mauricio Pochettino: Cavan Sullivan ready for USMNT debut
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said 16-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan is ready to play for the USMNT during the current international window, but was non-committal as to what role he would play in Saturday's friendly against Peru.
stories.body:
ORLANDO -- United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said 16-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan is ready to play for the USMNT during the current international window, but was noncommittal as to what role he would play in Saturday's friendly against Peru.

Sullivan has garnered the most attention on the current squad, even as 13 players that were part of the World Cup are also on the current roster.

This is due not only to his age, but also his recent performances for the Philadelphia Union, which have seen him score six goals and add eight assists in his last eight league games.

That has led to a tidal wave of anticipation to see what Sullivan can do at international level.

Pochettino said earlier this month that he and the staff needed to be "careful" in how they manager the young attacker. He was circumspect in his assessment of Sullivan at Friday's pre-match news conference.

"If we only talk about his performance, he's doing really well in his club in Philadelphia. Talking only about that, I think he's ready, but the rest of the players too," Pochettino said about Sullivan. "He's mature enough on the field."

Pochettino also praised the entire group for how they performed in training this week, and lauded the vitality that the youngsters have brought to the group.

"They have talent, and they are showing the real talent," Pochettino said of the young players. "They have an amazing capacity and quality. And then the energy was amazing. It's very contagious, that energy."

Pochettino added that he will use a mix of youth and experience against Peru, and he'll take the data from training to determine who is ready to play and who isn't.

"When we observe the player, maybe some players need more time, maybe not to play the first game or the second, maybe the third or maybe some player training with us is enough and maybe they don't need to go to play," Pochettino said. "I think it's so important to provide the chance if they are ready."

The USMNT manager said he'll be looking at a variety of other factors as well in terms of deciding what constitutes "ready."

He indicated he's been spending much of the week getting to know the players off the field as well as on. He's observed how the new players adapt to the environment, especially when the staff sets the tone early.

"I think if the young kids arrive in an environment that they smell respect, they smell the discipline, the normal discipline in a team that plays soccer, I think they are very natural," he said.

"I think what we need to, that was our plan is to create an environment that they can feel natural. We want them to behave in a natural way because they are intelligent, they're smart and they perceive and feel in the way that they need to act when they arrive."

Pochettino's assessment included getting the young players to get up on stage at a team dinner, one at a time, and sing a song in front of the team and staff.

"In all these types of things, you start to see their personality, their character, capacity to move," Pochettino said. "And then when they start to train, how the senior players respect them and start to play together and see how they move, how they talk, how they communicate, that's key. Then of course you need to talk with them and say, you feel that you are ready or not? But I think it's good to ask them, but at the same time it's to perceive and to read all this type of situation to be sure that they can go."

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

stories.body:
This is it, the weekend when we decide the two teams that will battle it out for the 2026 NRL premiership, and we have been presented with two cracking games to determine the grand finalists. On Friday night we have an attacking masterpiece when the Dolphins host the Roosters, before Sunday sees the giant-killing Knights facing the biggest giant of them all.

Good luck with your tips.

Friday, September 25
Dolphins vs. Sydney Roosters
Suncorp Stadium, 7:50pm (AEST)

Salesi Foketi 12. Siua Wong 13. Victor Radley Bench:14. Connor Watson 15. Angus Crichton 16. Nat Butcher 17. Spencer Leniu 18. Hugo Savala 19. Cody Ramsey Reserves: 22. Benaiah Ioelu

Officials

Referee: Adam Gee Touchies: Phil Henderson, Tyson Brough

Bunker: Ashley Klein

Prediction: The Dolphins were very impressive two weeks ago against the Warriors, restricting them to one try, before unleashing their signature attacking blitz after the break. Previously this season they have allowed teams to get away to big head starts before mounting their fightback, a ploy which just won't stand up in the finals. They appear to have taken note and their defensive work in New Zealand was outstanding. They will need to be at their very best once more against the Roosters, who have the attacking flair to cause them plenty of problems.

The Roosters were simply too good for the Sharks last week, after going very close to beating the Panthers the week before. They have plenty of experience across the park, with Daly Cherry-Evans putting in a much better performance against the Sharks in combination with the hard running Hugo Savala. Outside those two, the Roosters backline bristles with attacking weapons, with Robert Toia and Mark Nawaqanitawase in unstoppable form, James Tedesco always lurking, and Sam Walker returning at halfback.

But, as we all know, the backs don't win the big games, they just determine the score, and the Roosters have a pack that is the match of any in the league. Naufahu Whyte, Lindsay Collins and Siua Wong were at their destructive best against the Sharks. Add the menace of Victor Radley and Spencer Leniu, plus the returning Angus Crichton, and there isn't a weakness across the middle or on the edges.

The Dolphins will have to match the Roosters forwards, with Thomas Flegler, Tom Gilbert, Max Plath, Kulikefu Finefeuiaki, Ray Stone and Francis Molo all in for a big night. If they can negate the Roosters pack, we all know how devastating the Dolphins halves and backs can be.

On paper this is very difficult to pick. It is one of those games that might come down to a key error, a moment of madness, the luck of the bounce or the whims of the referee's six again calls. Whoever wins, we are sure to be treated to an entertaining clash.

Tip: Dolphins by 10

PointsBet odds: Dolphins $1.74 (-2.5 $2) Roosters $2.10 (+2.5 $1.83)

Penrith Panthers vs. Newcastle Knights
Accor Stadium, 4pm (AEST)
Panthers: 1. Dylan Edwards 2. Thomas Jenkins 3. Blaize Talagi 4. Casey McLean 5. Brian To'o 6. Jack Cole 7. Nathan Cleary 8. Moses Leota 9. Mitch Kenny 10. Lindsay Smith 11. Isaiah Papali'i 12. Liam Martin 13. Isaah Yeo Bench: 14. Jack Cogger 15. Scott Sorensen 16. Liam Henry 17. Billy Phillips 18. Luke Garner 21. Freddy Lussick Reserves: 22. Izack Tago

Knights: 1. Kalyn Ponga 2. Dominic Young 3. Dane Gagai 4. Bradman Best 5. Greg Marzhew 6. Fletcher Sharpe 7. Sandon Smith 8. Tyson Frizell 9. Phoenix Crossland 10. Cody Hopwood 11. Jermaine McEwen 12. Francis Manuleleua 13. Mathew Croker Bench: 14. Harrison Graham 15. Lachlan Crouch 16. Pasami Saulo 17. Dylan Lucas 18. Fletcher Hunt 19. Thomas Cant Reserves: 20. Kyle McCarthy

Officials

Referee: Gerard Sutton Touchies: Matt Noyen, Daniel Luttringer

Prediction: The best team of the 2026 season meets the hottest team of the 2026 finals in what should be another great game in front of a large crowd in Homebush.

The Panthers didn't have it all their way two weeks ago when defeating the Roosters, they were well-matched and needed a wobbly Nathan Cleary field goal to break a late deadlock. Cleary has been the focus ever since, as first he avoided suspension for a dangerous contact charge, and then set about rehabilitating an injured foot. The Panthers have proven they can win games without Cleary, but his coolness under pressure is invaluable in the biggest games.

The Knights are playing with the casino's money at this stage. After finishing last in 2025, making the finals surpassed anyone's expectations. To be playing in the Preliminary Final is an incredible achievement for coach Justin Holbrook and his team, especially considering they are without star half Dylan Brown. They simply have to keep playing the way they have been playing. Fast moving defence, free flowing ball movement from anywhere on the field, and total belief in their ability to beat anyone. Phoenix Crossland, Fletcher Sharpe, Kalyn Ponga, Bradman Best, Dan Gagai, Dom Young, the Knights have weapons across the field. Without Jacob Saifiti, they are a little light on up front, but veteran Tyson Frizell has stepped up in the middle and the Knights back-row ranks, strengthened now by the surprise return of Dylan Lucas, have been simply brilliant.

The big question is; can the Knights execute their attacking style against the best defence in the business? They played just the once this season, with the Panthers winning 44-12. We know how good the Panthers are. We have seen them dominate the big games for years. Cleary and Dylan Edwards orchestrating the attack, Isaah Yeo and Liam Martin leading the defence. The Panthers are the best team in the competition for good reason and they stand between the other three teams and the premiership title. I think they'll return to the big dance this year.

Tip: Panthers by 14

stories.headline: Guardians clinch 3rd straight AL Central crown with 11-5 win over Royals
stories.summary: — Once again, the Cleveland Guardians are division champs.
stories.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — Once again, the Cleveland Guardians are division champs.


Patrick Bailey and Brayan Rocchio each hit two of Cleveland's five home runs as the Guardians beat the Kansas City Royals 11-5 on Saturday night to clinch their third straight AL Central title.


Cleveland's victory coupled with Chicago's 9-6 loss to Colorado gave the Guardians (85-76) a two-game lead over the second-place White Sox (83-78) with one game remaining in the regular season on Sunday.


José Ramírez and the Guardians are assured the No. 2 seed in the American League playoffs and a first-round bye into a best-of-five Division Series. They will have five days off and then home-field advantage against the winner of a best-of-three Wild Card Series between the No. 6 seed White Sox and either Houston or Texas — whichever one wins the AL West on Sunday.


------

stories.headline: Brisbane Lions produce stuff of football immortality to claim three-peat
stories.summary: The Brisbane Lions etched their name into football folklore winning a third successive premiership, and their stunning Grand Final victory may never be bettered for drama or resilience, writes Rohan Connolly.
stories.body:
There's barely enough superlatives to describe a team good enough to win three premierships in a row. But what about one which not only achieves a three-peat, but does it the hard way three years straight, and just for good measure pulls off the most insane comeback in Grand Final history in the third and final leg?

That's the stuff of football immortality. And that's where Brisbane stands right now, having become only the second club in VFL/AFL history to win a second flag hat trick, following Melbourne in the mid-1950s.

The Demons, though, were dominant right through their second three-flag run between 1955-57. Brisbane has had to pull rabbit after rabbit out of the hat, in 2024 coming from fifth to victory, and last year bouncing back from a qualifying-final belting.

And now, this. Just three weeks ago, the Lions were absolutely smashed by Sydney to the tune of 53 points in a qualifying-final defeat which might have destroyed a team made of lesser stuff.

But what happened subsequently may never be bettered for drama or resilience in the midst of a finals campaign.

First, the Lions recovered their composure quickly enough to put Adelaide to the sword in a semifinal. Last week, they survived a withering Hawthorn comeback, trailing with little more than a minute left when Hugh McCluggage's tackle on Jarman Impey got them over the line.

That would have been more than enough September heroics to make this premiership very special regardless of what happened on Grand Final day. But now we have a win in the most important game of all which will be very hard to top.

A good 45 minutes after the final siren, it was still almost impossible to believe. With only four minutes 18 seconds left to play, Brisbane trailed by 17 points.

Remember that the biggest margin overhauled at three-quarter time of a Grand Final is only 23 points, in 1984. And Essendon had that deficit erased within eight minutes. How Brisbane conjured this Houdini trick is already the stuff of football legend.

Make no mistake. While Carlton's famous comeback from 44 points down at halftime of the 1970 Grand Final against Collingwood remains the gold standard of premiership-deciding revivals, this one, given the lateness of the hour, doesn't pale much in comparison.

The incredible Lions peeled off the last four goals of the game in just 250 seconds. The first, from Charlie Cameron didn't even provoke that much excitement from most of the 100,023 assembled, such was the feeling Fremantle was about to break its premiership duck.

That changed dramatically, however, when Zac Bailey snapped an amazing goal from a thicket of congestion with only another 24 seconds of play having elapsed. And then came Logan Morris.

Brisbane is replete with players who can have done very little throughout the course of a game and still win it. This week, it was the 21-year-old's turn.

Morris had had just eight disposals for 1.1 when, with 90-odd seconds left, he took the single most important mark of the game, a strong contested grab in front of Oscar McDonald. From 45 metres and with ice flowing through his veins, Morris put the Lions in front for the last time.

If that wasn't enough, he made sure of this famous win with a beautiful curling right foot snap from 35 metres. Seven points the difference now, just eight seconds left and game, set and match.

They just don't know how to quit, these Lions. They didn't when they overhauled a seven-goal deficit in a 2024 semifinal on their way to the first leg of this three-peat. They climbed off the canvas again that year's preliminary final.

Last week, they appeared to have blown another preliminary final until conjuring two goals in the last minute. And now a trick to top perhaps anything we've seen on the Grand Final stage.

"We probably thought it was starting to slip away, no doubt about it," Brisbane co-captain Hugh McCluggage told ESPN in the jubilant Lions' rooms after the game. "But we saw last week, this group just finds a way when it gets tough, and in a way it just felt like it was meant to be today after last week."

The sounding of "Wharfie Time" after Patrick Voss appeared to have clinched the premiership for the Dockers might have been a red rag to a bull for the Lions, but McCluggage said the incredible resolve goes back a lot further than that.

"We've done a lot of work over 10 years building our connection, building our brotherhood for moments like that," he said. "And it's a lot of butcher's paper sessions in the offseason, and days toiling down at Coorparoo in the heat, and it all pays off on days like this."

Coach Chris Fagan, sitting among the three premiership cups now literally with his fingerprints all over them, mirrored McCluggage's doubts with less than four-and-a-half minutes left on the clock.

"I thought we were in a little bit of trouble," he told ESPN with characteristic understatement. "The rate at which we were scoring during the game, it didn't look like it was going to happen. But, you know, we've got our strategies in place where if we've got to win the game, we'll roll the dice a little bit and try a few things. We're fortunate that we got the ball out in the middle, which is something we didn't really do all day.

"I just think over time we've just developed a great belief in ourselves. I feel like we're never out of it. So today was sort of like when it all came together, I suppose."

To say that sounded like someone reflecting on the culmination of a long-term project come to a successful conclusion might be an overstatement, but if Fagan does decide to pull the pin on the coaching caper, would any many man ever have gone out more on top than he?

"Oh well, I've been doing it for 10 years," he said. "It takes a lot out of you. I haven't made up my mind yet, but I sort of always had this idea that it would be good to walk away when you're on top rather than walking away when you're going no good at all."

No chance of that now. And what of the team he'd be leaving behind? They'll be in good hands whoever happened to take the reins. Because that coach will know first and foremost that not only is he in charge of the most talented and successful list in the AFL, he'll also be at the helm of a group that just doesn't know how to give up.

You can read more of Rohan Connolly's work at FOOTYOLOGY.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Liverpool eye winger Kevin Schade
stories.summary: Arsenal and Liverpool are upping their interest in Brentford's Kevin Schade, while the rest of Europe chases center backs. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Arsenal and Liverpool have identified Brentford's Kevin Schade as a potential addition to their squads, while the rest of Europe chases new center back options.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- There is increasing interest in Brentford winger Kevin Schade from Arsenal and Liverpool, according to Sky Sports. Brentford have held initial talks with the Germany international about extending his contract to see off that interest, with the aforementioned pair being the most serious about signing the 24-year-old when the summer transfer window drew to a close, although Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are also admirers. Schade has entered the last two years of his current deal and Brentford are keen to offer him improved terms.

- Inter Milan center back Alessandro Bastoni has re-emerged as a transfer option for Barcelona, while Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester City also retain an interest in him, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old was the topic of serious interest during the summer, but Inter remained firm on their valuation of close to £70 million for the Italy international. Chelsea would benefit from his ability to play in a back three, while Liverpool and City are looking at him as they prepare to eventually lose Virgil van Dijk and Rúben Dias.

- Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City are all keen on a potential deal for versatile Atlético Madrid midfielder Marcos Llorente, whose contract expires in the summer, according to TEAMtalk. Madrid are in talks with the 31-year-old over fresh terms and there is confidence within the Spanish club that an agreement will be reached. The situation has still attracted interest from the Premier League, with the trio of giants assessing whether Llorente could become available.

- Real Madrid are keeping an eye on Stuttgart center back Finn Jeltsch, reports Spanish newspaper AS. Madrid have signed Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté in the last two summer transfer windows but continue their efforts to strengthen the heart of their defence, and they are now monitoring several players from around the world. Jeltsch, 20, received his first Germany call-up from Jürgen Klopp this international window having joined Stuttgart from Nurnberg in January 2025.

- Liverpool are very satisfied with Ronald Araújo during his loan from Barcelona and could trigger their option to permanently sign the defender for €55 million, reports Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo. The Uruguay international has played seven matches for the Reds, five of those coming as a starter, but he is already convincing the club and Andoni Iraola. The versatility displayed by the 27-year-old to play both right-back and centre-back has also caught the eye.

Other rumors
- Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur have all been contacted by intermediaries about the potential availability of Barcelona attacking midfielder Dani Olmo. (TEAMtalk)

- Alejandro Balde could leave Barcelona in the January transfer window with Manchester United interested in the left back. (Mundo Deportivo)

- Juventus' priority left back options are RB Leipzig's David Raum and Crystal Palace's Tyrick Mitchell. (Tuttosport)

- AC Milan remain interested in Goncalo Inacio despite being unable to sign the center back from Sporting CP during the summer transfer window. (Tuttosport)

- Roma want to sign Frosinone winger Giorgi Kvernadze in January but face potential competition from Hull City and Borussia Dortmund. (Corriere dello Sport)

- AC Milan will allow the contracts of Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek to run down, and the former could even be offloaded in January. (La Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa have made enquiries over the availability of Al Ahli midfielder Valentin Atangana. (L'Equipe)

- Lazio defender Patric's free transfer to Al Ittifaq is at the final stage, with personal terms agreed on a contract that will run until 2028. (Nicolo Schira)

- Napoli are not satisfied with the performances of Lorenzo Lucca and Noa Lang, so they could depart in January. (Nicolo Schira)
